A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DISTA-Net, and their main text, equations, figures and tables are readable and matchable. However, v1 includes supplementary Sections 1–5 and Figures 6–7, whereas v2 ends with references while repeatedly referring to supplementary material that is not supplied. Appendix-level comparison is therefore incomplete.

before.justification: v1 reports original CSIST-100K experiments, component and sampling-grid ablations, and supplementary stage-count and branch-coefficient analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds an original comparison using YOLOv11 after reconstruction.

M1.justification: The iterative updates, dynamic transform, threshold generator and losses remain aligned. Algorithm 1 and the explicit final threshold convolution document operations already described in v1. However, v1 describes a structurally symmetric inverse transform, while v2 explicitly says symmetry is unnecessary. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the implemented architecture or corrects its description.

E1.justification: Both evaluate simulated CSIST-100K images containing 1–5 overlapping targets and the same sub-pixel unmixing task. The new detector-pipeline experiment reuses these infrared data; no additional dataset, population or input environment is reported.

E2.justification: Table 1 drops HiT-SIR and HiT-SRF while retaining HiT-SNG. Figure 5 adds EGASR and HiT-SNG to its visual comparison. The new pipeline experiment compares DISTA-Net + YOLOv11 against SRFBN + YOLOv11 and CFGN + YOLOv11. CTNet's changed citation does not introduce a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds an evaluation procedure using YOLOv11 after reconstruction, with the super-resolution methods retrained on infrared data and unmixing ground truth. The existing dataset split, sampling ratios, batch size, six-stage configuration, intensity cutoff and principal evaluation metrics remain unchanged as reported.

E4.justification: The component and sampling-grid analyses remain, and v2 adds a detector-pipeline analysis examining the role of reconstruction versus subsequent detection. However, v1's detailed stage-count and branch-coefficient sweeps in supplementary Section 4 and Figure 7 have no supplied v2 counterpart, despite retained references to them. Their retention or revision cannot be established.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports independent-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces PSNR and SSIM values throughout the retained learned-method comparisons while preserving localization scores. DISTA-Net changes from PSNR 37.8747 to 38.3825 and SSIM 99.79 to 0.9887; the SSIM change is not merely rescaling. Its PSNR is now below ISTA-Net+ (38.4998) and FISTA-Net (38.4773), and its SSIM ties ISTA-Net+. Tables 2–3 add threshold-specific AP results, while Table 2 removes computational-cost entries. The new YOLOv11 pipelines report 47.82 for DISTA-Net, 45.74 for SRFBN and 46.71 for CFGN. These are revised or newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting method improvements.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the maximum sub-pixel quantization deviation from sqrt(2)D/n to sqrt(2)D/(2n). It also identifies sigma_PSF squared, rather than sigma_PSF, as the diffusion variance. The main sparse-reconstruction derivation remains unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Both retain the claimed first deep-learning approach to CSIST unmixing, adaptive convolution and thresholding contributions, and the CSIST-100K/CSO-mAP/GrokCSO ecosystem. The abstract, introduction and conclusion preserve the same broad contribution and performance claims.

C2.justification: v2 uses the 0.236-pixel quantization bound at c=3 to justify emphasizing AP-20 and AP-25, replacing v1's emphasis on stricter-threshold performance. It qualifies the previously claimed highest reconstruction scores and interprets the new detector experiment as showing that unmixing supplies the dominant benefit and simple thresholding can separate reconstructed peaks.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 makes the learnable stage parameters explicit, and Equation 19 specifies the threshold combination. Conversely, Table 2 no longer supplies ablation parameter counts and FLOPs. v1's closed-form initialization and additional metric/toolkit documentation are in its appendix; v2 points to unavailable supplementary details. The full change in reproducibility information cannot therefore be determined.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations for D2ANet, MirSAM and a fully 1×1 convolutional super-resolution network. It also cites the contextual-transformation paper for CTNet instead of the EDSR paper. The central positioning against binary target detection and static deep unfolding remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the introduction, contribution list, dataset description, experimental settings and conclusion, standardizes DTG terminology, corrects headings and adds acknowledgments. The main six-section organization and much of the prose remain aligned; the unavailable supplement prevents verifying claimed relocations there.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different conference-style layout, replacing the branded title/abstract panel and changing typography and spacing throughout. Figures 1 and 4 are revised, Algorithm 1 is added, and Figure 5 expands and moves. Table 2 replaces computational columns with threshold-specific AP columns, and Table 3 adds AP-10 and AP-15 columns.

improvement.justification: The corrected quantization bound, explicit algorithm, finer AP breakdowns and detector comparison improve clarity and supporting evidence. However, v2's referenced supplement is unavailable, ablation cost information disappears, and the widespread PSNR/SSIM replacements lack an explanation establishing their cause or correctness. These limitations prevent a reliable net assessment of overall quality from the supplied PDFs.
